newsitem.title: FRANCE: GEC Alsthom partners study merger with Framatome.
newsitem.headline: GEC Alsthom partners study merger with Framatome.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom and Britain's General Electric Co Plc said on Friday they were studying a possible merger between their joint venture engineering company GEC Alsthom and France's state-controlled nuclear power plant manufacturer Framatome.
The French government, which six years ago forced Alcatel to cede majority control of Framatome, reversed its stand and on Friday gave its blessing to the merger study.
Alcatel, which currently holds 44 percent of Framatome, had long said that it wanted to regain control or might pull out.

A merger between GEC Alsthom, whose engineering record includes France's high-speed trains, and Framatome would create a group with annual sales of around $15 billion and 90,000 employees worldwide, Alcatel and GEC said in a statement.
"It is envisaged that shares in the new group would be held by the present shareholders of the companies involved, bearing in mind their respective contributions," they said.
Framatome is one of the world's leading builders of power stations and suppliers of nuclear fuel.

"There's industrial logic behind the deal. Most of Alcatel's big competitors have the capability to offer nuclear as well as traditional power plants. This would allow Alcatel to compete on the same footing," Paribas analyst Christopher Tucker said.
Shares in Alcatel Alsthom were up 2.20 francs at 393 francs, bucking a declining trend on the Paris bourse whose CAC-40 index was down 0.13 percent at 1030 GMT.

Framatome is controlled by state shareholders that include the Atomic Energy Commission's industrial subsidiary CEA Industrie with 36 percent and utility Electricite de France which has around 10 percent.

The finance ministry, saying it had authorised the merger discussions, said a deal would allow the "creation of a group offering a complete range of conventional and electrical nuclear plants and have a size enabling it to compete with its international rivals."

However, given Framatome's key role in the French nuclear power industry, the state's approval would hinge on "appropriate control guarantees" and the centre-right government would be vigilant in defending the national interest, the ministry said.
Such concerns drove a previous Socialist government in 1990 to push Alcatel to reduce its stake in Framatome, but Alcatel has been unhappy with the situation ever since.
"A 44 percent shareholding is either too much or not enough," Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk said earlier this year. "It does not make any sense to stay at that level."
Analysts said it was too early to calculate the financial implications of a merger between GEC Alsthom and Framatome as no details were issued on Friday.

Alcatel Alsthom is also planning to bid for Thomson SA, a state-owned electrical equipment group slated for privatisation this year. French media-to-missiles conglomerate Lagardere is also bidding for Thomson.
